title: Readiness Signal Capture — Weekly Infrastructure Brief
content:
Meeting: Infrastructure weekly — readiness / capacity signals
Date: 2027-11-02
Facilitator: Leah Martinez
Attendees: Leah M., Arjun P., Maya C., Samir G., Toni A., Keiko (SRE on-call), Rami (capacity planning)
Slack: #infra-gpu-ops, pings to @capacity-leads

Top-line summary (TL;DR):
- Overall fleet is at 88% committed capacity versus forecast for this week; usable spare (non-preemptible) is ~6% across primary regions. Demand spikes from batch customers in APAC caused transient queueing yesterday (2027-11-01 22:10 UTC) — root cause: unexpected model rollout (cust-B) that did not declare a traffic spike in the deployment policy.
- Priming experiment (small-batch prewarm) gained ~12–18% tail-latency improvement for short-chat workloads in eu-west-1; cost delta small (0.6% extra hours) and team recommends expanding to us-west-2 pilot.
- Immediate risk: H100 shortage in asia-sg for next three weeks due to vendor lead times; plan to shift low-priority reserved allocations to A100 in asia and route latency-tolerant traffic to edge pools.

Observations and signals this week:
1) Regional snapshots (2027-11-02 04:00 UTC):
   - us-west-2: inventory 320 H100 (active), 120 A100 (active), 18 preemptible nodes; utilization 93% peak, mean p95 latency for text-generation 210ms.
   - eu-west-1: inventory 200 H100, 90 A100; utilization 79%, mean p95 latency 180ms, priming pilot showed reduced cold-start 250ms->210ms on sample traces.
   - asia-sg: inventory 96 H100, 30 A100; utilization 97% (hot), p95 latency 360ms for long-context prompts. Spare capacity effectively 3% once reserved pools accounted.

2) Demand drivers identified:
   - Customer-B heavy model rollout at 2027-11-01 21:50 UTC; their traffic pattern had large-batch fanout (concurrent 400 sessions) causing queue depth and preemption churn. Ticket: JIRA-INFRA-4127.
   - Two internal experiments (research) ramped up request rate without capacity flagging — need stricter gating on traffic declarations.

3) Prewarming/priming experiments:
   - Experiment: continuous prefix priming for 1min prior to predicted traffic windows (target short chat models).
   - Result (sample size 48k requests): median cold-start reduction 9%, p95 reduction 12–18% in eu-west-1. CPU/GPU hours increased by ~0.6% for region during priming windows.
   - Action: expand to us-west-2 for 72h pilot next week. Owner: Arjun P. (runbook + kickoff)

4) Supply risk and mitigation:
   - H100 procurement delay — estimated delivery slippage to 3–4 weeks for next procurement tranche.
   - Mitigation plan: temporarily reclassify 20% of reserved trial capacity to A100-backed variants (model-quantization Q3) and shift non-latency-critical inference to edge pools. Owner: Rami.

5) Incidents and blips:
   - 2027-11-01 22:10 UTC: transient queue growth in asia-sg; impact window ~9min; observed ~0.8% increase in error-rate for hosted-api customers in region. Postmortem draft started (INFRA-4127).
   - 2027-10-31 16:00 UTC: scheduler misclassified some primed workers as idle, leading to premature scale-down; root cause: TTL threshold mismatch in autoscaler config. Patch merged in PR #581 (deploy next deploy window).

Capacity forecast and planning notes:
- Seven-day lookahead (baseline forecast vs committed):
   * us-west-2: forecast +6% week-over-week growth (expected holiday ramp in client X). Recommended to reserve +10% burst pool for 72h windows.
   * eu-west-1: steady; priming expansion should reduce tail pressure; monitor p99 error budget.
   * asia-sg: forecast +14% due to retained customer promotions; high risk of hitting soft-guard rails — propose moving low-priority queued workloads to us-west-2 overnight windows (local night in APAC -> US morning).
- Cost/econ note: shifting some H100-workloads to A100 increases token-cost by ~1.2–1.8% per-million tokens for heavy long-context runs; but keeps 99.9% availability SLAs intact.

Operational playbook updates (short bullets):
- Autoscaler TTLs: bump min-idle TTL from 90s -> 150s for regions with high churn until next scheduler release. (Owner: Toni)
- Priming runbook: add precondition check for declared traffic window and opt-out tag for research runs. (Owner: Arjun)
- Capacity alert tuning: add an "unexpected-model-rollout" alert that triggers when a customer increases concurrency >200 within <5min without a matching deployment ticket. (Owner: Maya)

Open questions / discussion items for next sync:
- Do we enforce a hard gating policy that blocks customer rollouts unless they set a traffic declaration flag? Pros/cons and rollout plan. (Risks to PLG experience vs operational stability)
- How aggressive should we be about automated model-variant fallback to A100? Should fallback be opt-in per customer?
- Evaluate whether priming should be a paid feature (Redwood Optimize) vs platform-level default for certain SKUs.

Action items (owner / due):
- Arjun P.: prepare us-west-2 priming pilot runbook + schedule (due 2027-11-05).
- Rami: publish H100 mitigation mapping (which customer pools move to A100, expected token-cost delta per pool) (due 2027-11-04).
- Toni: deploy autoscaler TTL bump to staging and run soak tests (due 2027-11-03).
- Maya: implement the unexpected-model-rollout alert prototype in Datadog (alert id: infra-proto-2027-11) and link to PagerDuty (due 2027-11-06).
- Leah: consolidate postmortem skeleton for INFRA-4127 and assign reviewers (due 2027-11-03).

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Consider lightweight "rollout tax" flag in console — customers explicitly indicate expected concurrency; without flag, platform will throttle deploy or require canary. Could be part of onboarding checklist.
- Think about automated suggestion in Console: "Switch to primed nodes for short-chat models — saves p95 latency at small cost increase" (opt-in toggle).

References and links:
- Priming experiment dashboard: CONFLUENCE-Infra/priming-pilot/results (link above)
- Related PRs: github.com/redwood-infra/priming-scripts/pull/92, /pull/96 (staging tweaks)
- Postmortem draft: JIRA-INFRA-4127 (linked)
- Slack huddle: #infra-gpu-ops thread ts 1698868200

Appendix — sample metric snapshot (text representation):
- region, active-GPUs, utilization_peak, spare_pct, p95_ms
- us-west-2, 440, 93, 6, 210
- eu-west-1, 290, 79, 15, 180
- asia-sg, 126, 97, 3, 360

Next meeting: 2027-11-09, same time, focus: priming pilot results + H100 procurement update.
